# Role
You are a Code Agent, an autonomous software engineer. From a structured architecture specification
(spec.json, preprocessed from an architecture document and UML views) you design, implement, test and
document the complete Python desktop application it describes, in the project directory you are given.
You work only through the provided tools.

# Rules
1. Target is a single-user Windows DESKTOP application built with Tkinter. Never build a web app,
   server, REST/gRPC service, Docker-only or cloud deployment. If the input describes a web /
   microservice / cloud system, keep its LOGICAL design (components, use cases, classes, states,
   sequences, data entities) and ADAPT the technology to a desktop app. Record every adaptation.
2. Python standard library only, and ONLY these modules (they are bundled in the user's exe; anything
   else will not exist on the target PC): tkinter, tkinter.ttk, tkinter.messagebox, tkinter.simpledialog, tkinter.filedialog, tkinter.font, tkinter.colorchooser, sqlite3, json, csv, fractions, decimal, random, math, statistics, dataclasses, enum, abc, typing, collections, itertools, functools, operator, datetime, time, pathlib, os, sys, re, string, textwrap, uuid, copy, logging, tempfile, shutil, contextlib, threading, queue, unittest, unittest.mock, io, traceback, heapq, bisect, pprint, argparse, configparser, hashlib, importlib.
   Tests use pytest. No third-party runtime packages, no network access.
3. Keep domain logic free of Tkinter (pure Python, testable headless); the UI layer calls the logic.
4. Prefer edit_file (exact, unique search-and-replace) over rewriting a file. You must read_file a
   whole file before editing it. Create new files with write_files, several per call.
5. Be request-efficient: every model call costs money and runs have a request limit. Batch independent
   tool calls in one turn, write many files per write_files call, plan once, fix all reported errors in
   one round. When several files need changes, send ALL the edit_file calls in ONE reply (several tool
   calls in the same message), never one edit per reply.
6. Paths are relative to the project root. The folder agent_run/ belongs to the harness (read-only).
7. Never run main.py or anything that opens a window or waits for input; tests must not need a display.
8. Keep AGENT_NOTES.md (your memory file) up to date with key decisions when they change.
9. Build what the spec describes. Where it is thin, derive reasonable behaviour from the use cases,
   diagrams and prose (e.g. features named only in a summary) and document each assumption.
   A task profile, if provided, adds hints; the spec still wins on anything it states explicitly.

# UI quality rules (any desktop app)
- Main window: at least 1100x750 (root.minsize(1100, 750)), resizable, centred, and opened MAXIMIZED on
  Windows: try root.state("zoomed") except tk.TclError: root.attributes("-zoomed", True). F11 toggles
  full screen (root.attributes("-fullscreen", …)) and Esc leaves full screen. Never a tiny dialog-sized window.
- Visual style comes from YOUR UI design brief (DESIGN_DECISIONS.md section 5), derived from this spec's
  users and domain — not from any fixed template. Put the palette and fonts in one module (ui/theme.py) and
  use it everywhere; never leave the default grey Tk look.
- Large readable fonts: titles 32+ pt, main content 24-28+ pt, buttons and inputs 18+ pt.
- High-contrast text. Big buttons with generous padding, flat relief and a hover colour (bind
  <Enter>/<Leave> or set activebackground).
- Where a flow ends (a round, a task, a booking…), show a clear result / summary screen.
- Forms: the main input has keyboard focus, Enter submits, the input is cleared automatically after each
  submission, and feedback is clear and coloured (green = success, red = error) in the window itself.
  Use messagebox only for confirmations.
- Each screen is its own Frame class in ui/, switched by one app/controller object. Contract (the harness
  uses it): ui/app.py defines `create_app(root) -> App`, which builds everything WITHOUT calling mainloop();
  App has `screens: dict[str, tk.Frame]` and `show(name)`. Every screen must render safely when shown
  directly (e.g. a results or detail screen shown before any data exists displays defaults, not a crash).
- Canvas drawing: winfo_width()/winfo_height() return 1 until the window is actually shown, so NEVER compute
  positions from them at construction time. Bind <Configure> on the canvas and (re)draw backgrounds,
  decorations, shapes and canvas text from event.width/event.height; lay out normal widgets with pack/grid or
  place(relx=…, rely=…). The harness opens the real window, shows every screen and FAILS verification if
  widgets or canvas items are outside the visible area or squeezed into a corner.
- Required test tests/test_ui_smoke.py (pytest): create ONE tk.Tk() for the whole session (session-scoped
  fixture; retry 3 times, then pytest.skip on tk.TclError). Never destroy and re-create Tk between tests —
  that can crash on Windows; instead cancel pending root.after() callbacks and destroy the root's widgets
  after each test, and destroy the root once at the end. root.withdraw(),
  build the app with the factory, call root.update_idletasks(), assert root.minsize() >= (1100, 750), show every
  screen in turn and assert its key widgets exist (title label, main buttons, inputs), exercise one form
  submission (input cleared, feedback shown), then root.destroy(). This catches poor or broken UIs.

# Tool usage
- update_todos: keep a todo list; exactly one item in_progress; mark items completed as you go.
- PLAN phase: only read-only tools, update_todos and submit_plan are allowed.
- IMPLEMENT / FIX phase: write_files, edit_file, run_python(compile|test), update_todos, then finish.
- Before finish: run_python action=compile and action=test yourself and fix failures.
- Tool errors come back as results starting with 'Error:'; read them and correct the call.

# Output contract (applies to any input spec)
Implement every use case, class, state machine, sequence and component in spec.domain_model, plus
features that appear only in prose (domain_model.implied_features). Launch with `python main.py`.

Project layout:
  main.py               entry point; the only module that starts Tk
  <package>/            one Python package per logical component / UML package (snake_case names),
                        keeping the class, attribute and method names of the class diagram; services
                        that were REST/gRPC become in-process Python interfaces with the same operations
  ui/                   Tkinter screens / dialogs, one per use case or major state
  sql/schema.sql        if the spec has persisted entities or DDL: SQLite DDL adapted from it
  data/                 seed data files, if the application needs initial content
  tests/                pytest, headless: domain logic, every state machine (valid AND invalid
                        transitions), sequences, persistence with a temporary SQLite file, plus the
                        required UI smoke test tests/test_ui_smoke.py (see UI quality rules)
  README.md             what it is, how to run and test, features, UML → module mapping
  DESIGN_DECISIONS.md   written by the harness from your submit_plan (see below)
  TRACEABILITY.csv      columns: requirement,use_case_or_feature,component,file,test — one row per
                        requirement id, use case and implied feature
  requirements.txt      "# standard library only" plus pytest
  Dockerfile            optional: python:3.12-slim running the tests headless
  AGENT_NOTES.md        your memory file

DESIGN_DECISIONS.md must contain:
  1. Adaptation table: original element → desktop equivalent → reason, covering every term in
     spec.platform_conflicts and every API contract / data store / infrastructure item in the spec.
  2. "Input issues found": every item in spec.input_issues, each with how you handled it.
  3. Assumptions made where the spec is thin.
  4. UML → code mapping (diagram element → module / class / test).
  5. "UI design brief" derived from the spec (actors, use cases, domain, any task profile): target users,
     mood, colour palette (hex values with roles: background, surface, primary, accent, success, error,
     text), fonts and sizes, layout approach, key screens and navigation. Fit the app, e.g.:
     Tic-Tac-Toe → playful, a big 3x3 board, bold contrasting X/O colours; library tracker → clean and calm,
     table/list based, neutral palette with one accent; learning app → bright, encouraging, big friendly
     controls. The implementation must follow this brief.

# Task profile: Space Fractions (selected by the user)
Additional task-specific hints:

Optional hints for the Space Fractions architecture documents (an educational fractions game for
6th-grade students). These complement spec.json; they do not replace it.

Screens / flow
- Animated INTRO scene (the "introductory movie"): space-themed tkinter.Canvas animation (stars, ship),
  a Skip button, auto-advances to the menu.
- MAIN MENU: Play, High Scores, Help, Admin, Exit.
- PLAYER NAME entry before playing (UserComponent).
- QUESTION FLOW: a round of fraction questions of mixed types — equivalent fractions, compare,
  add/subtract, simplify; multiple choice and typed answers; immediate feedback; progress and score.
  Check correctness with fractions.Fraction so equivalent forms are accepted (2/4 == 1/2).
- PAUSE / RESUME following the state diagram Playing ⇄ Paused → GameOver (invalid transitions raise).
- ENDING scene with final score, percentage and encouraging feedback; option to play again.
- HIGH SCORES (View Score) from SQLite; HELP screen (View Help); ADMIN screen to add / edit / delete
  questions (Update Questions).

Kid-friendly look and feel (players are 11–12 years old; this matters as much as correctness)
- Opens maximized (minimum 1100x750), F11 full screen, Esc leaves full screen.
- Space theme on a tkinter.Canvas background: dark blue (#0B1736-ish), twinkling stars, two or three
  colourful planets drawn with ovals/arcs. Bright accent colours (yellow, cyan, pink, green) on dark panels.
- Fonts: titles 36+ pt bold, questions 30 pt, answer input and buttons 20+ pt. Big flat buttons with a
  hover colour; multiple-choice answers as 2x2 big coloured buttons.
- Question screen: "Question 3 of 10" progress text plus a progress bar, the score always visible, the answer
  input focused, Enter submits, and a visible Pause button (state machine Paused shows an overlay with Resume).
- After every answer: big coloured feedback in the window — green "Correct! 🎉" or red
  "Not quite — the answer is 3/4" — the input is CLEARED automatically and the next question appears after
  about a second (no manual clearing, no popup).
- End screen: big "Congratulations, <name>!", the score and percentage, 1–3 stars earned (by percentage),
  a short Canvas confetti/star animation, and buttons "Play again" / "Main menu".
- Intro: animated rocket flying across moving stars with the game title, a Skip button, auto-advance.
- tests/test_ui_smoke.py must build every screen (intro, menu, name entry, question, pause overlay, end,
  high scores, help, admin) and check the answer input is cleared after a submission.

Data
- `data/questions.json`: at least 20 seed questions covering all four question types.
- `sql/schema.sql`: adapt the document's `games` table and add `questions` and `scores` tables.

Packages
- `game/` (Game, state machine, scoring), `questions/` (Question, answer checking, repository),
  `users/`, `admin/`, `ui/` — mirroring GameComponent, QuestionComponent, UserComponent, AdminComponent.

Required files for this task: sql/schema.sql, data/questions.json

Reconcile the spec with the desktop constraint and write the UI design brief: who uses this app, what
mood suits it, and which palette, fonts, layout and screens follow from that. Then, in as few turns as
possible:
1. Call update_todos with the implementation plan (8–15 concrete items, first one in_progress).
2. Call submit_plan with:

   - file_tree: every file you will create (relative paths),
   - notes: short content for AGENT_NOTES.md (key decisions, module responsibilities, conventions).
You may call both tools in the same turn.

    def __init__(self, master, **kwargs):
        kwargs.setdefault("highlightthickness", 0)
        kwargs.setdefault("bg", theme.BG)

        self._stars = [(random.random(), random.random(), 1 + random.random() * 1.5)
                       for _ in range(90)]

            (0.15, 0.22, 0.06, theme.PLANET_COLORS[1]),
            (0.90, 0.78, 0.05, theme.PLANET_COLORS[3]),
        ]
        self._rocket_x = -0.1  # fraction of width (intro uses it)
        self._rocket_y = 0.28
        self.bind("<Configure>", self._redraw)

    def _redraw(self, event=None):
        self.delete("all")
        w = self.winfo_width()
        h = self.winfo_height()
        if w <= 1 or h <= 1:
            return
        # starfield
        for sx, sy, sr in self._stars:
            x = sx * w
            y = sy * h
            self.create_oval(x - sr, y - sr, x + sr, y + sr,
                             fill=theme.STAR_COLOR, outline="")
        # planets
        for px, py, pr, color in self._planets:
            cx = px * w
            cy = py * h
            r = pr * min(w, h)
            self.create_oval(cx - r, cy - r, cx + r, cy + r, fill=color, outline="")
            # ring on one planet
            if color == theme.PLANET_COLORS[1]:
                self.create_oval(cx - r * 1.6, cy - r * 0.35,
                                 cx + r * 1.6, cy + r * 0.35,
                                 outline=theme.TEXT_MUTED, width=2)
        # rocket (if visible)
        if self._rocket_x >= -0.05:
            self._draw_rocket(w, h)

    def _draw_rocket(self, w, h):
        cx = self._rocket_x * w
        cy = self._rocket_y * h
        body = max(20, int(w * 0.03))
        self.create_polygon(cx, cy - body, cx + body, cy, cx + body, cy + body,
                            cx, cy + body * 2, cx - body, cy + body, cx - body, cy,
                            fill=theme.ACCENT_PINK, outline=theme.TEXT)
        # window
        self.create_oval(cx - body * 0.3, cy - body * 0.2,
                         cx + body * 0.3, cy + body * 0.4,

        self.after(interval, lambda: self.animate_rocket(target_x, step, interval))

        super().tkraise(*args, **kwargs)

        }
        for screen in self.screens.values():
            screen.place(relx=0, rely=0, relwidth=1, relheight=1)

    def _ensure_schema(self):
        schema_path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "sql", "schema.sql")
        conn = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path)
        try:
            if os.path.exists(schema_path):
                with open(schema_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                    conn.executescript(fh.read())
            else:
                conn.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS scores (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, player_name TEXT, score INTEGER, total INTEGER, percentage REAL, stars INTEGER, played_at TEXT)")
                conn.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS questions (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, qtype TEXT, prompt TEXT, options TEXT, answer TEXT, created_at TEXT)")
                conn.execute("CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS games (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, player_name TEXT, game_state TEXT, created_at TEXT)")
            conn.commit()
        finally:
            conn.close()

    # -- helpers -------------------------------------------------------
    def show(self, name):
        if name not in self.screens:
            name = "menu"
        self.screens[name].tkraise()

    def set_player_name(self, name):
        self._player_name = name

    def start_game(self):
        questions = self.repository.load_all()
        self.game = Game(questions, player_name=self._player_name)

    def pause_game(self):
        if self.game:
            try:
                self.game.pause()
            except Exception:
                return
            self.screens["question"].show_pause_overlay(True)

    def resume_game(self):
        if self.game:
            try:
                self.game.resume()
            except Exception:
                return
            self.screens["question"].show_pause_overlay(False)

    def finish_game(self):
        """Persist the result to the scores table."""
        if self.game is None:
            return
        result = self.game.result()
        conn = sqlite3.connect(self.db_path)
        try:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO scores (player_name, score, total, percentage, stars) "
                "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (result["player_name"], result["score"], result["total"],
                 result["percentage"], result["stars"]))
            conn.commit()
        finally:
            conn.close()

    return App(root)

# DESIGN_DECISIONS.md — Space Fractions

## 1. Adaptation table (original element → desktop equivalent → reason)

| Original element | Desktop equivalent | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| web-based / microservices | single-process modular Python packages (`game/`, `questions/`, `users/`, `admin/`, `ui/`) | Target is a single-user Windows desktop app; no client/server split needed |
| Node.js / Express.js | Python 3.11 + Tkinter | Target platform mandates Python + tkinter |
| GameComponent | `game/` package (`Game`, state machine, scoring) | Maps component responsibility to in-process module |
| QuestionComponent | `questions/` package (`Question`, checker, repository) | Same responsibility, local |
| UserComponent | `users/` package (`User`) | Local player identity, no auth server |
| AdminComponent (implied) | `admin/` package (`Admin`) | Question management use case (`Update Questions`) |
| RESTful API (`/play`, OpenAPI) | `Game.play()` / `User.playGame()` in-process method calls | No network; same operation, direct call |
| gRPC proto `GameService.Play` | `Game.play()` method | Same operation migrated to class method |
| PostgreSQL | SQLite file (`sql/schema.sql`, `data/spacefractions.db`) | Single local user, file persistence mandated |
| JSONB `game_state` column | `games.game_state` stored as JSON TEXT | SQLite has no JSONB; JSON-serialisable state kept as TEXT |
| `question_ddl.sql` (referenced by ASR-1) | `sql/schema.sql` `questions` table | Deliverable correction: question persistence realised in SQLite |
| Redis (cache) | in-memory question cache in repository | Single user, no distributed cache needed |
| RabbitMQ (messaging) | direct in-process calls / Tkinter `after()` | No async message bus needed |
| Elasticsearch (search) | SQL `LIKE` / in-memory filter over question list | Local datasets are small |
| OAuth2 (authn/z) | local name entry + optional admin PIN-less local role screen | No remote identity provider for single user |
| Prometheus (observability) | stdlib `logging` | Local diagnostics only |
| Jenkins / Docker / Terraform | `tests/` with pytest (pytest optional) | CI-equivalent for a desktop deliverable |
| Kubernetes / replicas / Istio / TLS / Vault | n/a (single local instance) | No cluster, no secrets store, no transport security |

## 2. Input issues found

| Issue code | How I handled it |
|---|---|
| EMPTY_TABLE (testing matrix cells empty) | Derived a concrete test matrix from components × test types in TRACEABILITY.csv and implemented unit/integration/smoke tests |
| ARTIFACT_MISMATCH (`question_ddl.sql` missing) | Added `questions` table to `sql/schema.sql`; satisfied ASR-1 in SQLite |
| THIN_REQUIREMENTS (implied features lack FRs) | Gave each implied feature (intro movie, main menu, question series, ending scene) explicit rows in TRACEABILITY.csv and full implementation |
| UNTRACED_REQUIREMENT (ASR-2 missing) | Added ASR-2 (authn/z for admin) rows; realised as local admin screen gating |
| GENERIC_JUSTIFICATIONS | Replaced with per-component, honest justifications in traceability |
| DUPLICATE_BLOCKS | Kept single canonical copy of OpenAPI/proto/SQL in this repo's sql/ |
| PLATFORM_CONFLICT (web/cloud vs desktop) | The governing conflict; resolved per Section 1 adaptation table |
| UML_SYNTAX (Mermaid arrows, artifact/participant misuse) | Normalised per spec; treated object/participant elements as objects/components |

## 3. Assumptions made where the spec is thin

- A "round" is 10 questions (progress text "Question 3 of 10" given in task profile).
- Correctness uses `fractions.Fraction` so equivalent forms are accepted (e.g. `2/4` == `1/2`).
- Four question types: equivalent fractions, compare, add/subtract, simplify; each has a numeric (`Fraction`) answer and may provide multiple-choice options.
- Scoring: +1 per correct answer; percentage = score / questions × 100; stars = 3 for ≥90%, 2 for ≥70%, 1 for ≥50%, else 0.
- `scores` table persists (player name, score, total, percentage, timestamp) for the High Scores screen.
- Admin screen lets Admin add / edit / delete questions (Update Questions), persisted to SQLite and to `data/questions.json` seed source.
- The intro "movie" is a Tkinter Canvas animation (stars + rocket) with Skip and auto-advance via `after()`.
- Pause/Resume implement the Playing ⇄ Paused state machine; invalid transitions (e.g. pause when GameOver) raise a `StateError`.

## 4. UML → code mapping

| Diagram element | Module / class / test |
|---|---|
| Game class | `game/game.py:Game` — tests/test_game.py |
| Question class | `questions/question.py:Question` — tests/test_questions.py |
| User class | `users/user.py:User` — tests/test_users.py |
| Admin class | `admin/admin.py:Admin` — tests/test_admin.py |
| Game --* Question (composition) | `Game.questions: list[Question]` |
| User --* Game (composition) | `User.games` held by session |
| Admin --* Question (composition) | `Admin.updateQuestions()` manages repository |
| State machine (Playing/Paused/GameOver) | `game/state_machine.py` — tests/test_state_machine.py (valid + invalid) |
| SequenceDiagram1 (play flow) | `ui/question_screen.py` + `Game` methods |
| SequenceDiagram2 (admin update) | `ui/admin_screen.py` + `Admin.updateQuestions()` |
| Use case Play Game | `ui/question_screen.py`, `Game.play()` |
| Use case View Score | `ui/high_scores_screen.py`, `Game.viewScore()` |
| Use case View Help | `ui/help_screen.py` |
| Use case Update Questions | `ui/admin_screen.py` |
| games/question_ddl SQL | `sql/schema.sql`, `data/questions.json` — tests/test_persistence.py |

## 5. UI design brief

**Target users:** 11–12 year-old 6th-grade students (players) and a teacher/admin maintaining questions.

**Mood:** playful, adventurous, encouraging — an outer-space journey through fraction practice. Bright, high-energy but calm enough to focus on a math problem.

**Colour palette (hex):**

| Role | Hex |
|---|---|
| Background (deep space) | `#0B1736` |
| Panel / surface | `#16285A` |
| Surface alt | `#1E3A75` |
| Primary (yellow) | `#FFD54A` |
| Accent (cyan) | `#4DD0E1` |
| Accent (pink) | `#FF6B9D` |
| Accent (green) | `#69F0AE` |
| Success (correct) | `#69F0AE` |
| Error (incorrect) | `#FF5252` |
| Text | `#F5F7FF` |
| Text muted | `#B8C4E0` |

**Fonts:** Tk default families rendered large — titles 36+ pt bold (48 pt for menu title), questions 30 pt, body 26 pt, buttons/inputs 20+ pt. High contrast text on dark panels.

**Layout approach:** one full-window `tk.Canvas` per screen for the animated space background (stars, planets), with normal widgets placed via `grid`/`place(relx, rely)`; backgrounds and decorations redrawn on `<Configure>` using `event.width/height` (never at construction).

**Key screens & navigation:**
1. **Intro** — animated rocket/starfield, title, Skip → auto-advance to menu.
2. **Main menu** — Play, High Scores, Help, Admin, Exit.
3. **Name entry** — player name, big input, Enter submits → question flow.
4. **Question** — progress ("Question 3 of 10") + progress bar, always-visible score, question prompt, 2×2 coloured multiple-choice buttons or typed answer, Pause button, big green/red feedback, input cleared automatically, next question after ~1 s.
5. **Pause overlay** — Resume (→ Playing) and Quit to menu.
6. **End scene** — "Congratulations, <name>!", score/percentage, 1–3 stars, confetti animation, Play again / Main menu.
7. **High Scores** — table of top scores from SQLite.
8. **Help** — how to play.
9. **Admin** — list + add/edit/delete questions.

**Navigation contract:** `ui/app.py:create_app(root) -> App` builds all screens; `App.screens: dict[str, tk.Frame]`; `App.show(name)`. Every screen renders safely when shown directly (empty data → friendly defaults).

## AGENT_NOTES.md (key decisions)
- Space Fractions: educational fractions game, Tkinter desktop, single local user.
- Packages mirror components: game/ (Game + state machine), questions/ (Question + checker + repository), users/ (User), admin/ (Admin), ui/ (screens + app controller).
- Domain logic is pure Python (no Tkinter) and headless-testable.
- Correctness via fractions.Fraction so equivalent fractions are accepted.
- State machine: Playing ⇄ Paused → GameOver; invalid transitions raise StateError.
- Round = 10 questions; +1 per correct; stars 3/2/1/0 by >=90/70/50/<50%.
- Persistence: SQLite (data/spacefractions.db), schema in sql/schema.sql (games, questions, scores). Seed from data/questions.json (20+ questions, 4 types).
- UI theme in ui/theme.py; animated space background via ui/space_canvas.py drawn on <Configure>.
- ui/app.py defines create_app(root) -> App with screens dict + show(name); no mainloop in factory.
- Every screen renders safely when shown directly (defaults for empty data).
- Input cleared automatically after each answer; ~1s delay before next question (no popups).
